youtube_description:
You're eating healthy and you're working out, but the scale will not move. It's almost certainly not your metabolism, your hormones or your genetics. You're eating more calories than you think, and untracked eating is invisible even to the person doing it. I was 200 pounds at 5'7" and I would have told you I ate pretty well.

Track your calories from a photo with AI:
https://absbyai.com/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=longform&utm_content=ro14-not-losing-weight

The 4 calorie leaks:
1. You're not tracking. With AI, you take a photo of your plate and it takes two seconds.
2. Weekend blowouts. One big Friday dinner and a lazy Saturday erase your whole weekday deficit.
3. Liquid calories. Coffee drinks, juice, smoothies, protein shakes, alcohol. My rule: if it has calories, don't drink it.
4. Invisible calories. Cooking oil poured straight from the bottle (a tablespoon of olive oil is 120 calories), dressing, sauces, bites of your kids' food, three nuggets over the trash can. 400 invisible calories a day is 40 pounds a year.

Then the 4 hidden reasons you're eating them: a fat girlfriend or a fat wife who doesn't care about her health, fat friends who pressure you to overeat, not being on tirzepatide or another GLP-1 (I'm not a doctor, so talk to yours, but Zepbound helped me get abs), and bad sleep. Sleep is not a fat loss secret. It drains the willpower you need to say no.

My simple system: fast until 2 PM with 2 to 4 cups of black coffee. Photograph every meal and every drink, especially on the weekend. Weigh yourself daily and watch the 7-day trend. Spend less time with the people pulling you down. Protect your sleep. You are not stuck. You are guessing. Give it 30 days of honest tracking.
